nl.statement: A finite population of \(G\in2\mathbb N\) mutually isolated groups, each of common size \(n\in4\mathbb N\), observed at the endpoints of \(B\) two-period assignment blocks. Every unit \(i\in\mathcal I_n\) of every group \(g\in\mathcal G_G\) at every period \(t\le 2B\) carries a fixed schedule-indexed potential outcome \(Y_{gti}:\mathcal H_{2B}\to[-M,M]\) on the within-group treatment-and-saturation history space \(\mathcal H_{2B}=(\mathcal D\times\mathcal Q)^{2B}\), with \(\mathcal D=\{0,1\}\) and \(\mathcal Q=\{q_L,q_H\}=\{1/4,3/4\}\); \(\mathcal H_t\) is the corresponding history space through period \(t\). Under ordinary nonanticipation together with the imposed lag-one finite-memory restriction, the block endpoint of a two-period block whose exposure is held at \((d,q)\) is the sustained-exposure endpoint \(Y_{gbi}(d,q)\in[-M,M]\). The potential outcomes are fixed: the only randomness is the experimenter's two-stage assignment, and \(\mathcal F_b\) is generated by assignments and observed endpoints through block \(b\). Each group carries a prespecified centered baseline score \(H_g\) with \(|H_g|\le K_H\) and \(\sum_g H_g=0\); observed block-endpoint group means \(\bar Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{gb}\) and their grand mean \(\bar Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_b\) feed the predictable balance score \(V_{gb}\) with loading \(\lambda\), whose complete-randomization imbalance variance \(\sigma_b^2\) is confined to a window \([c_\sigma,C_\sigma]\). Growth of \(G\) relative to \(B\) is otherwise unconstrained between \(c_\rho\) and \(C_\rho\). The structural class \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\) collects the arrays satisfying these conditions, and \(\mathcal W^{AB}\subseteq\mathcal M_{G,B}\) is the explicit alternating-block witness family. — Search trace: `npm run search -- "finite population fixed potential outcomes randomization design" --cluster experimentation` + `lean_local_search FiniteDesign / toMeasure / prodDesign`; scanned Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/{DesignCore,PotentialOutcome,Exposure,FiniteDesignMeasure,Product,TwoStage}.lean and Causalean/Experimentation/{TwoStageInterference,UnknownInterference,ExposureMappingInterference}/. Result: `Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.FiniteDesign` (DesignCore.lean) is EXACTLY this world's probability layer -- a pmf on a finite assignment space with `E`/`Var`/`Cov`/`ind`/`Pr` finite-sum algebra (`Cov_linear_comb`, `Var_linear_comb`, `E_sum`) and the measure bridge `FiniteDesign.toMeasure` (`FiniteDesignMeasure.lean`) for the asymptotic statements. REUSED, not rebuilt. The fixed schedule-indexed outcome family `Y_{gti} : H_{2B} -> [-M,M]`, the two-period-block sustained-exposure reduction `Y_{gbi}(d,q)`, the predictable balance score `V_{gb}`, and the class carrier are define-local (a history-indexed 2B-period schedule with lag-one memory has no Causalean analogue: `PotentialOutcome.ProperlySpecified` is single-period exposure factorization, a PARTIAL fit only). Analogous module for the schedule layer: Causalean/Experimentation/TwoStageInterference/{Basic,Stratified}.lean (`WAssign`, `stratExpo`, `exists_strat_factor`) -- adapt from a single-period within-group exposure to the 2B-period history with the lag-one collapse. `c_\rho`/`C_\rho` are declared relative-growth constants that the delivered results deliberately do NOT constrain (the note's headline is that no restriction on G/B is needed); they are bound here as inert design constants and must not be smuggled into any theorem hypothesis. `\mathcal M_{G,B}` is realized as the `def:model-class` structure and is the ambient carrier every class-scoped statement quantifies over; `\mathcal W^{AB}` is the `def:adaptive-witness` construction.

At each block \(b\), conditionally on \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\), the first stage draws a balanced saturation sign vector \(x_b\) from the support \(\mathcal X_G=\{x\in\{-1,1\}^G:\sum_gx_g=0\}\). The uniform balanced-sign reference law is \(P_0(x)=\binom{G}{G/2}^{-1}\); the raw balance statistic \(Z_b(x)=G^{-1/2}\sum_gx_gV_{gb}\) is exactly standardized to \(W_b(x)=Z_b(x)/\sigma_b\), so \(\operatorname{Var}_0\{W_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1}\}=1\). The soft radial weight \(f_{\eta,\kappa}(w)=\eta+(1-\eta)e^{-\kappa w^2}\in[\eta,1]\) with floor \(\eta\in(0,1)\) and curvature \(\kappa>0\) tilts \(P_0\) into the predictable soft-rerandomization law \(P_{\mathrm{RR},b}(x\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=P_0(x)f_{\eta,\kappa}\{W_b(x)\}/C_b\), normalized by \(C_b=\mathbb E_0[f_{\eta,\kappa}\{W_b\}\mid\mathcal F_{b-1}]\in[\eta,1]\). The realized sign fixes the group saturation \(Q_{gb}=q_H\) if \(x_{gb}=1\) and \(q_L\) otherwise. Conditionally on \(x_b\), the second stage draws exactly \(nQ_{gb}\) treated units uniformly without replacement in each group, independently across groups, and holds both stages fixed across the two periods of the block. The within-group exposure probability is \(p_{1q}=q\), \(p_{0q}=1-q\); \(I_{gbi,dq}\) indicates the realized exposure cell, whose conditional first- and second-order inclusion probabilities \(\pi_{gbi,dq}\) and \(\pi_{k\ell,b}\) are known and logged by the randomizer. — Search trace: `npm run search -- "two-stage compound design conditional within-group randomization" --cluster experimentation`, `npm run search -- "complete randomization inclusion probability pair"`, `lean_local_search compound / prodDesign / completeRandomization_incl / completeRandomization_incl_pair / tilt / reweight`; scanned Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/{TwoStage,Product,ProductVariance,CompoundVariance,Designs/CompleteRandomization,Designs/Stratified,Exposure}.lean and Causalean/Experimentation/Sequential/AdaptiveDesign.lean. FOUND and REUSED: (i) `compound D1 D2 : FiniteDesign (Omega1 x (forall i, alpha i))` is exactly the block's stage-1-then-independent-within-group structure, with the tower `E_compound_tower`, the total-variance law `Var_compound_eq_tower`, the stage-2 collapse `E_compound_factor`, and `Var_prod_linear_comb`; (ii) `completeRandomization n1 hn : FiniteDesign {S : Finset V // S.card = n1}` IS the uniform fixed-count law -- instantiated at `V = G-groups, n1 = G/2` it IS `P_0` on the balanced-sign support, and at `V = I_n, n1 = n*q` it IS the fixed-count second stage, with the first- and second-order inclusion probabilities already proved as `completeRandomization_incl` and `completeRandomization_incl_pair` (these directly supply `p_dq` and the within-group entries of `pi_{kl,b}` used by lem:pair-probability-control and thm:studentizer). NOT FOUND, hence define-local (small, build-inline): a soft-tilt combinator `softTilt D f : FiniteDesign Omega` with `p x = D.p x * f x / D.E f` -- `lean_local_search tilt / reweight` returned nothing in Causalean, and `lean_loogle`/`lean_leansearch` for a Mathlib pmf reweighting turned up only `PMF`-level `Measure.withDensity`, which is the wrong (measure-theoretic, un-normalized) abstraction for this finite-sum layer. Also NOT FOUND: a predictable chain of finite designs across B blocks -- `Causalean/Experimentation/Sequential/AdaptiveDesign.lean` (`AdaptiveExperiment`, `HasOverlap`, `propensity_pos_of_overlap`) is measure-theoretic over a Mathlib `Filtration`, a different abstraction from this finite-sum design layer; the B-block predictable chain is define-local, built by iterating `compound` over the block prefix so that `F_{b-1}` is realized as the realized path prefix (the same conditioning idiom Causalean's TwoStageInterference uses). Recorded as bypass-justified for `AdaptiveDesign.lean` only: the artifact is a purely finite, algebraic randomization layer, while that module is the measure-theoretic superpopulation flavor. The soft tilt and complement symmetry live in Helpers/SoftTilt.lean; the balanced-sign uniform-perfect-matching representation lives in Helpers/PerfectMatching.lean.

The causal target and its estimator live on the four exposure cells \((d,q)\in\mathcal D\times\mathcal Q\) with the fixed direct-and-spillover contrast coefficients \(c_{0q_L}=(-1/2,-1/2)^\top\), \(c_{1q_L}=(1/2,-1/2)^\top\), \(c_{0q_H}=(-1/2,1/2)^\top\), \(c_{1q_H}=(1/2,1/2)^\top\). The finite-population sustained-exposure means are \(\mu_{dq}\); the block target is \(\tau_b\in\mathbb R^2\) and the estimand is \(\tau=(\tau_D,\tau_S)^\top=B^{-1}\sum_b\tau_b=\sum_{d,q}c_{dq}\mu_{dq}\). The logged-probability Horvitz--Thompson estimators are \(\widehat\mu_{dq}\), the block vector \(\widehat\tau_b\), and the headline \(\widehat\tau=B^{-1}\sum_b\widehat\tau_b\). Within a group the saturation-specific causal score is \(m_{gbq}\), its Horvitz--Thompson counterpart \(\widehat m_{gbq}\), the centered sampling error \(e_{gbq}=\widehat m_{gbq}-m_{gbq}\) with conditional covariance \(T_{gbq}\), and the high-versus-low score difference \(a_{gb}=m_{gbq_H}-m_{gbq_L}\). The normalized block error \(R_b=\sqrt G(\widehat\tau_b-\tau_b)\) splits into the balanced-sign component \(A_b=G^{-1/2}\sum_gx_{gb}a_{gb}\) and the within-group component \(U_b=2G^{-1/2}\sum_ge_{gb,Q_{gb}}\), with covariance pieces \(K_b\), the complete-randomization benchmark \(\Sigma_{b,0}\), the soft-rerandomization covariance \(\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}\), and the score-on-imbalance projection loading \(\beta_b\). — Search trace: `npm run search -- "Horvitz Thompson estimator inverse probability weighted exposure mean unbiased" --cluster experimentation`, `npm run search -- "two-stage direct spillover effect estimator"`, `lean_local_search E_htTotal / htMean / muTrue / Cov_linear_comb`; scanned Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/HT/{Estimator,Unbiased,Variance}.lean, Causalean/Experimentation/TwoStageInterference/{Unbiased,Effects,Variance,BetweenGroupEffect}.lean, Causalean/Experimentation/ExposureMappingInterference/. Result: PARTIAL fits only, so define-local. `htTotal`/`htMean`/`htEffect` and `E_htTotal`/`E_htMean`/`E_htEffect` (HT/Estimator.lean, HT/Unbiased.lean) are the scalar, single-period, static-propensity HT layer; the artifact's estimator is R^2-valued over four exposure cells with a triple (block, group, unit) index and PREDICTABLE (history-dependent) inclusion probabilities, so the conclusion does not type-match and this is not a discharge. ANALOGOUS MODULES to adapt (recorded for F3): Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/HT/Unbiased.lean `E_htTotal` for the indicator-forced substitution `I*Yobs = I*y` then division by pi (the technique behind prop:exact-unbiasedness, needing only the extra conditional-on-F_{b-1} layer supplied by `E_compound_factor`); Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/HT/Variance.lean `Var_htTotal_cov` for the double-sum-of-covariances form of the block covariance (equation (8) of thm:studentizer); Causalean/Experimentation/TwoStageInterference/BetweenGroupEffect.lean `Var_estDirect` for the two-stage between/within split of an EFFECT estimator. The vector-valued (R^2) lifting is the gap F3 must bridge -- `FiniteDesign.Cov_linear_comb`/`Var_linear_comb` (DesignCore.lean) are scalar and get applied coordinatewise. Mathlib-side check `lean_leansearch "Horvitz-Thompson design-based estimator"` / `lean_loogle "inclusion probability"`: nothing; Mathlib has no design-based survey-sampling layer.

The Gaussian comparison objects are the centered pairs \((A_b^\star,W_b^\star)\in\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R\) and \((R_b^\star,W_b^\star)\), each carrying the exact conditional \(P_0\)-covariance of its discrete counterpart and supported on that covariance range when the covariance is singular. The history-uniform transport modulus is a deterministic sequence \(\varepsilon_G\downarrow0\). The standard-normal soft-tilt shrinkage constant is \(v_{\eta,\kappa}=\{\eta+(1-\eta)(1+2\kappa)^{-3/2}\}/\{\eta+(1-\eta)(1+2\kappa)^{-1/2}\}\in(0,1)\). The limiting covariances are \(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}\) (soft rerandomization), \(\Omega_{\mathrm{CR}}\) (complete randomization), and the precision-gain matrix \(P\), the deterministic limit of \(B^{-1}\sum_b\beta_b\beta_b^\top\). — Search trace: `lean_local_search stdGaussian / multivariateGaussian / posSqrt / lambda1`, `lean_leansearch "centered Gaussian measure with given covariance on a finite dimensional space"`, `lean_loogle "Matrix.PosSemidef"`; scanned Causalean/Mathlib/{StandardGaussian,OperatorSqrt}.lean, Causalean/Mathlib/Analysis/{TwoByTwoSpectralRoots,SingularValueWeyl}.lean, Causalean/Stat/CLT/{ChiSquared,GaussianLimit,MultivariateCLT}.lean, Mathlib/Probability/Distributions/Gaussian/Multivariate.lean. REUSED: `Causalean.Mathlib.stdGaussian` (a mean-zero Gaussian on any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with `covarianceBilin_stdGaussian`, `isGaussian_stdGaussian`, `stdGaussian_mean`) plus `LinearMap.IsPositive.posSqrt`/`posSqrtCLM` (`posSqrt_mul_self`, `posSqrt_isPositive`) to realize the covariance-matched pair as `Sigma^{1/2} Z` -- this is exactly the singular-support construction the proof needs (the PSD square root exists without any positive-definiteness), so no eigenvalue lower bound is ever taken. `ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian` (Mathlib) supplies the N_2(0, Omega_RR) limit law object. `Causalean.Mathlib.Analysis.lambda1`/`lambda2`/`rootDiscriminant`/`lambda1_mul_lambda2`/`eigenvalue_eq_lambda1_or_lambda2` give the explicit ordered 2x2 spectrum used for lambda_min(Omega_RR) > 0 and det(P) > 0. Define-local (build-inline, small): `epsilon_G` as a deterministic modulus, `v_{eta,kappa}` as a closed-form scalar, and the covariance-range support predicate.

The observable studentizer is indexed by the block exposure-cell set \(\mathcal K_b=\mathcal G_G\times\mathcal I_n\times\mathcal D\times\mathcal Q\), whose element \(k=(g,i,d,q)\) carries the vector-valued outcome \(u_{k,b}=c_{dq}Y_{gbi}(d,q)\in\mathbb R^2\). The unordered impossible-pair set is \(\mathcal Z_b=\{\{k,\ell\}:k\ne\ell,\ \pi_{k\ell,b}=0\}\). The block estimator \(\widehat\Gamma_b\in\mathbb S^2\) is the pairwise Horvitz--Thompson covariance sum over the feasible pairs augmented by a diagonal Young completion over \(\mathcal Z_b\), whose deterministic excess is the positive-semidefinite completion bias \(D_b=(Gn^2)^{-1}\sum_{\{k,\ell\}\in\mathcal Z_b}(u_{k,b}+u_{\ell,b})(u_{k,b}+u_{\ell,b})^\top\). Averaging gives \(\widehat\Gamma=B^{-1}\sum_b\widehat\Gamma_b\), and clipping its two eigenvalues at the deterministic sequence \(r_B\downarrow0\) gives the invertible \(\widehat\Gamma_+\in\mathbb S_{++}^2\). At nominal noncoverage \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) the simultaneous Wald ellipse is \(\mathcal C_\alpha=\{t\in\mathbb R^2:GB(\widehat\tau-t)^\top\widehat\Gamma_+^{-1}(\widehat\tau-t)\le\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\}\). — Search trace: `npm run search -- "conservative variance estimator zero joint probability Young completion" --cluster experimentation`, `npm run search -- "spectral clipping eigenvalue floor two by two symmetric matrix"`, `lean_local_search htA2 / E_htVarEst_add_htA2_ge / lambda1 / chiSqDist`, `lean_leansearch "chi squared distribution quantile continuity point"`; scanned Causalean/Experimentation/ExposureMappingInterference/Variance/Conservative.lean, .../Asymptotics/{VarEstQuadBound,VarEstConsistencyConditions}.lean, Causalean/Mathlib/Analysis/{TwoByTwoSpectralRoots,TwoByTwoSpectralProjector,SingularValueWeyl}.lean, Causalean/Stat/CLT/{ChiSquared,ChiSquaredProjection}.lean. REUSED: `Causalean.Stat.chiSqDist` with `stdGaussian_map_normSq` (the chi-squared law IS the pushforward of the squared standard-Gaussian norm) and `noAtoms_chiSqDist` (no atom at the positive quantile -- exactly the continuity point thm:wald-coverage needs at equation (22)); `Causalean.Mathlib.Analysis.lambda1`/`lambda2`/`rootDiscriminant_nonneg`/`lambda2_le_lambda1`/`lambda1_add_lambda2`/`lambda1_mul_lambda2`/`eigenvalue_eq_lambda1_or_lambda2` (TwoByTwoSpectralRoots.lean) give the explicit ordered 2x2 eigenvalues in closed quadratic form, which turns the spectral clipping at r_B and the Weyl-type step (15) of thm:studentizer into elementary algebra on the trace and discriminant rather than a general spectral-theorem argument; `topProjector`/`topProjector_isOrthogonalProjectorOntoTop` (TwoByTwoSpectralProjector.lean) gives the choice-free eigenprojector so the clipped matrix is defined without an arbitrary eigenvector sign. Define-local because Causalean's Young-completed estimator is scalar and static: `htA2` / `E_htVarEst_add_htA2_ge` / `htCovEstA` / `E_htEffectVarEstA_ge` (ExposureMappingInterference/Variance/Conservative.lean) is the SAME Young-inequality-on-the-zero-joint-pairs technique and is the ANALOGOUS MODULE F3 should adapt; the gap to bridge is (a) scalar -> 2x2 symmetric matrix conservativeness in Loewner order, (b) fixed -> predictable logged pair probabilities. Mathlib-side check `lean_loogle "Matrix.PosSemidef"` / `lean_leansearch "Loewner order inversion reverses"`: `Matrix.PosSemidef` and `Matrix.PosSemidef.det_nonneg` exist and cover the PSD algebra; the Loewner-inversion-reversal step (20) has no direct Mathlib lemma and is a small build-inline fact at 2x2 via the explicit roots.
Conditional on the finite population \(\{Y_{gti}:g\in\mathcal G_G,\ i\in\mathcal I_n\}\), the only randomness is generated by \(x_b\) and \(A_{gbi}\).

review.note: Lean ⇒ paper fails: the predicate never mentions x_b or A_gbi and permits realizedHistory to contain arbitrary randomness not generated by them; conversely, the NL condition alone does not state Lean's observed-outcome consistency equality.

standard.name: Finite-population randomization inference
standard.citation: Xinran Li and Peng Ding (2017), General forms of finite population central limit theorems with applications to causal inference, Journal of the American Statistical Association 112, 1759--1769.

nl.statement: For every unit, \(Y_{gti}\) is invariant to treatment and saturation assignments outside group \(g\).

review.note: The universal equality exactly says that changing any assignments outside group g while preserving group g's complete history leaves Y_gti unchanged.

standard.name: Partial interference across groups
standard.citation: Michael G. Hudgens and M. Elizabeth Halloran (2008), Toward causal inference with interference, Journal of the American Statistical Association 103, 832--842.

nl.statement: Within group \(g\), the endpoint response depends on the contemporaneous assignment vector only through the unit's own treatment \(d\) and the realized saturation \(q\).

review.note: Paper ⇒ Lean fails: besides holding the within-group past fixed and reducing the contemporaneous vector to own treatment and saturation, Lean permits arbitrary changes to all future periods and all other groups, thereby additionally assuming nonanticipation and partial interference.

standard.name: Stratified interference
standard.citation: Michael G. Hudgens and M. Elizabeth Halloran (2008), Toward causal inference with interference, Journal of the American Statistical Association 103, 832--842.

nl.statement: For every \(t\leq2B\), if \(h,h'\in\mathcal H_{2B}\) agree through period \(t\), then \(Y_{gti}(h)=Y_{gti}(h')\); assignments after period \(t\) do not affect the period-\(t\) endpoint.

review.note: Paper ⇒ Lean fails at the declared within-group history domain: Lean represents global histories and requires equality when only group g agrees through t, so it additionally imposes invariance to arbitrary assignments in every other group.

standard.name: Nonanticipating potential outcomes
standard.citation: Iavor Bojinov, Ashesh Rambachan, and Neil Shephard (2021), Panel experiments and dynamic causal effects: A finite population perspective, Quantitative Economics 12, 1171--1196.

nl.statement: For every \(2\leq t\leq2B\), if \(h,h'\in\mathcal H_{2B}\) agree at periods \(t-1\) and \(t\), then \(Y_{gti}(h)=Y_{gti}(h')\) regardless of the remaining history entries.

review.note: Both directions fail: Lean additionally requires invariance to arbitrary histories outside group g, while its 0-based condition 2 ≤ t.val starts at paper period 3 and omits the paper-required period t=2 case (which is t.val=1).

nl.statement: Uniformly over \(b\in\mathcal B_B\) and realized \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\), \(c_\sigma\leq\sigma_b^2\leq C_\sigma\).

review.note: Paper ⇒ Lean after fixing one realized history, but Lean ⇒ paper fails because the predicate quantifies only over blocks for σsq : Fin B → ℝ and does not itself impose uniformity over realized histories; repair it to accept σsq : Ω → Fin B → ℝ and quantify ∀ w b.

standard.name: Finite-population nondegenerate variance condition
standard.citation: Xinran Li and Peng Ding (2017), General forms of finite population central limit theorems with applications to causal inference, Journal of the American Statistical Association 112, 1759--1769.

review.note: Entrywise convergence in design probability of the actual block-average covariance process to the deterministic Mat2 limit is equivalent to the stated finite-dimensional matrix convergence in probability.

standard.name: Predictable quadratic-variation stabilization
standard.citation: Xinran Li and Anqi Zhao (2026), Design-based theory for causal inference from adaptive experiments, arXiv:2602.21998.

review.note: For the real symmetric covariance matrix ΩRR, Matrix.PosDef ΩRR is equivalent to λ_min(ΩRR) > 0.

standard.name: Positive-definite target covariance
standard.citation: Xinran Li and Anqi Zhao (2026), Design-based theory for causal inference from adaptive experiments, arXiv:2602.21998.

review.note: Entrywise convergence in design probability of the actual complete-randomization block-average covariance to the deterministic Mat2 limit is equivalent to the stated finite-dimensional matrix convergence in probability.

standard.name: Finite-population covariance stabilization
standard.citation: Xinran Li, Peng Ding, and Donald B. Rubin (2018), Asymptotic theory of rerandomization in treatment--control experiments, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 115, 9157--9162.

review.note: Entrywise convergence in design probability of the actual average of β_bβ_bᵀ to the deterministic Mat2 limit P is equivalent to the stated finite-dimensional matrix convergence in probability.

nl.statement: \(\mathcal M_{G,B}=\{(Y,H):G\in2\mathbb N,\ B\in\mathbb N,\ n\in4\mathbb N,\ \text{assumptions }\texttt{ass:design-based-finiteness},\texttt{ass:partial-interference},\texttt{ass:stratified-interference},\texttt{ass:nonanticipation},\texttt{ass:finite-memory-lag-one},\texttt{ass:imbalance-variance-window}\text{ hold}\}\).

review.note: Paper membership implies the Lean fields can be instantiated, but Lean does not imply paper membership: `design` is an arbitrary finite law with no constraint tying its pmf to the conditional soft first stage or uniform exact-count second stage, and `G_even`/`n_four` also admit the zero-size cases.

nl.statement: At block \(b\), draw \(x_b\in\mathcal X_G\) with \(P_{\mathrm{RR},b}(x\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=P_0(x)f_{\eta,\kappa}\{W_b(x)\}/C_b\); set \(Q_{gb}=q_H\) for \(x_{gb}=1\) and \(q_L\) otherwise; then draw exactly \(nQ_{gb}\) treated units uniformly and independently within each group and hold both stages fixed for the two periods.

review.note: Every stated paper design is an instance of this compound tilt, but the converse fails because `P0`, `weight`, and every `secondStage` are arbitrary; Lean does not require balanced-sign support, the specified radial weight and normalizer, saturation-dependent uniform exact treatment counts, or two-period holding.
After unfolding `contrast` and `exposureMean`, Lean sums the four Boolean treatment-saturation cells with the stated two-component coefficients and sustained-exposure population means.

After unfolding `exposureMeanEstimator` and `cellIndicator`, Lean is exactly the four-cell contrast of the `(GBn)⁻¹` sum of observed endpoints times the exposure indicator divided by the logged inclusion probability.

The paper asserts `R_b = A_b + U_b`, while Lean only defines an auxiliary vector `blockScoreSplit := A_b + U_b`; unfolded `blockA` and `blockU` have the stated formulas, but this declaration does not assert their equality with `blockR`.

nl.statement: Represent the balanced three-vector \((a_{gb,1},a_{gb,2},V_{gb}/\sigma_b)\) by a uniform random perfect matching followed by independent pair orientations; target a history-uniform covariance-range comparison through smooth Lindeberg replacement, covariance interpolation, fourth-moment truncation, and a conditional characteristic-function augmentation for \(U_b\).

review.note: Paper ⇒ Lean by forgetting the random law and orientations, but Lean ⇒ paper fails: a fixed-point-free involution alone records neither uniform matching, independent pair orientations, the balanced-vector representation, nor the stated history-uniform comparison.
After unfolding the let-binding and real powers, Lean defines exactly ΔΩ = (1-vηκ)P with the stated numerator and denominator for vηκ.

nl.statement: \(\widehat\Gamma_b=(Gn^2)^{-1}[\sum_{k,\ell:\pi_{k\ell,b}>0}I_kI_\ell(\pi_{k\ell,b}-\pi_{k,b}\pi_{\ell,b})u_{k,b}u_{\ell,b}^\top/(\pi_{k\ell,b}\pi_{k,b}\pi_{\ell,b})+\sum_{\{k,\ell\}\in\mathcal Z_b}\{I_ku_{k,b}u_{k,b}^\top/\pi_{k,b}+I_\ell u_{\ell,b}u_{\ell,b}^\top/\pi_{\ell,b}\}]\), followed by block averaging and eigenvalue clipping at \(r_B\).

review.note: Paper ⇒ Lean after forgetting probability coherence, but Lean ⇒ paper fails because the model structure leaves pi and piPair arbitrary—including zero, negative, asymmetric, or design-inconsistent values—so the positive-pair split, denominators, and spectral clipping need not represent the paper's inclusion-probability estimator.
Unfolding matQuad and chiSquareQuantile2 gives exactly the set of t with GB(τ̂-t)ᵀΓ̂₊⁻¹(τ̂-t) ≤ χ²₂,1-α.

nl.statement: For \(G\in4\mathbb N\), represent the four sign pairs \((H_g,J_g)\in\{-1,1\}^2\) equally often and set \(\lambda=1\). On type A blocks take \((a_{Dg},a_{Sg})=(H_g,J_g)\) and \(L=0\); on type B blocks take \((a_{Dg},a_{Sg})=(J_g,H_g)\) and \(L=4\). Set \(\theta_g=4a_{Dg}\), \(\delta_g=L-\theta_g\), \(h_g=a_{Sg}/2+a_{Dg}-L/2\), and \(Y_{gbi}(d,q)=h_g+d(\delta_g+\theta_gq)\).

review.note: Paper ⇒ Lean for admissible signs, but Lean ⇒ paper fails: G,H,J are unrestricted, equal representation of the four ±1 sign pairs is absent, and the returned family contains no condition fixing λ=1.

nl.statement: For every finite \(G\), \(B\), and history, complement symmetry gives \(\Pr_{\mathrm{RR}}(Q_{gb}=q_H\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=\Pr_{\mathrm{RR}}(Q_{gb}=q_L\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=1/2\). Hence \(\pi_{gbi,dq}=p_{dq}/2\geq1/8\) and \(\mathbb E_{\mathrm{RR}}(\widehat\tau)=\tau\) exactly.

review.note: Paper does not imply Lean: the paper restricts to the complement-symmetric soft two-stage law, but Lean universally quantifies unrelated D, x, A, history, observed, and pi; for example, a singleton design with x constantly true and constant-zero outcomes satisfies every Lean hypothesis while its first raw conditional probability is 1 rather than 1/2. Add a non-laundering design-law premise or constructed carrier tying these objects to softTwoStageDesign and ensure conditioning is restricted to, or proved positive on, supported histories.

nl.statement: For every block, \(R_b=A_b+U_b\), \(\mathbb E(U_b\mid x_b,\mathcal F_{b-1})=0\), and the group summands of \(U_b\) are conditionally independent. Consequently \(\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}=\operatorname{Var}_{\mathrm{RR}}(A_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})+K_b\), the cross covariance is zero, and exactly the same \(K_b\) appears under \(P_0\).

review.note: Neither direction holds: `Mdl.design` is unconstrained rather than the stated soft two-stage law, Lean replaces conditioning on `(x_b, F_{b-1})` and conditional independence by history-only zero pairwise products, and its `P_0` covariance clause merely unfolds a hard-coded definition; constrain the design, state conditional factorization, and relate the covariance to an actual `P_0` law.

nl.statement: The block scores satisfy \(\mathbb E(R_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=0\), and \(\sqrt{GB}(\widehat\tau-\tau)=B^{-1/2}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_B}R_b\).

review.note: Paper ⇒ Lean fails because Lean claims conditional centering for an arbitrary `FiniteDesign`, without a premise tying `design`, `x`, `Aassign`, and `pi` to the paper's soft two-stage mechanism; add that design-law predicate, after which the coordinatewise centering and scaling identity match.

nl.statement: There exists a finite constant \(C_R\), independent of \(G\), \(B\), \(b\), and the history, such that \(\mathbb E_0\|R_b\|^4\leq C_R\) and \(\mathbb E_{\mathrm{RR}}(\|R_b\|^4\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})\leq C_R/\eta\).

review.note: Neither direction holds: Lean chooses `C_R` after fixing one `Mdl`, so it may depend on `G`, `B`, and the realized-history/design data, while both bounds use the same arbitrary `Mdl.design` and no `P_0` expectation appears; quantify one constant before the model array and supply distinct `P_0` and soft-tilted `P_RR` laws.

nl.statement: There is a constant \(C_\pi<\infty\), independent of block and history, such that for distinct groups \(g\neq h\), \(\left|\mathbb E_{\mathrm{RR}}(x_{gb}x_{hb}\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})\right|\leq C_\pi/G\). Therefore every feasible cross-group exposure-pair probability equals its product-marginal benchmark plus \(O(G^{-1})\) uniformly, while every feasible within-group pair probability is bounded away from zero.

review.note: Paper ⇒ Lean, but Lean ⇒ paper fails: C_pi and c_pair are chosen after one fixed Mdl and may depend on G and its arbitrary unconstrained pi/piPair tables, so Lean does not encode constants uniform across G or require the tables to be the soft-design inclusion probabilities; quantify an admissible design family before the constants and tie pi/piPair to softTwoStageDesign.

nl.statement:
For every sequence of finite-population designs belonging to \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\) along which \(B\to\infty\), with the admissible even value of \(G\) allowed to depend arbitrarily on \(B\) and in particular allowed to remain fixed, suppose separately that
\[
B^{-1}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_B}\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}\to_P\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\lambda_{\min}(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}})>0.
\]
Then
\[
\sqrt{GB}(\widehat\tau-\tau)=B^{-1/2}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_B}R_b\ \Rightarrow\ N_2(0,\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}).
\]
Thus the root-\(GB\) limit law requires no restriction on \(G/B\); it is derived from martingale centering, the uniform block fourth-moment bound, and the two displayed theorem-specific covariance conditions rather than from membership in the structural class.

review.note: Lean implies the paper result on the intended subclass, but the paper does not imply Lean: `BoundedLagOnePartialInterferenceClass` permits an arbitrary `FiniteDesign` and arbitrary `V`, `x`, `Aassign`, `pi`, and `piPair` without tying them to the stated predictable soft two-stage design, its logged inclusion probabilities, or sequence-uniform envelopes; add an exact design/well-formedness predicate with uniform array constants to the quantified domain.

nl.statement:
As \(G\to\infty\), uniformly over blocks and histories and without any restriction on \(G/B\), \(\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}=\Sigma_{b,0}-(1-v_{\eta,\kappa})\beta_b\beta_b^\top+o(1)\). Along every sequence with \(G\to\infty\) on which the complete-randomization, soft-rerandomization, and projection covariance stabilizations hold,
\[
\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{CR}}-(1-v_{\eta,\kappa})P.
\]
For every fixed contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}\), soft rerandomization has strictly smaller asymptotic variance than complete randomization if and only if \(c^\top Pc>0\).

review.note: Lean-domain → paper-domain fails: `Mdl.design` is an unconstrained `FiniteDesign` with no condition tying it to the paper's `softTwoStageDesign`, and the per-`N` fields `M`, `KH`, `cSigma`, and `CSigma` may vary despite being fixed uniform constants in the paper; add design-law coherence and common cross-`N` bounds, noting that `hWindow` merely duplicates each record's nonuniform `varianceWindow`.

nl.statement:
For every member of \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\) operated under the predictable soft two-stage design and every block,
\[
\mathbb E(\widehat\Gamma_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}+D_b,
\qquad D_b\succeq0.
\]
Along every sequence in \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\) with \(B\to\infty\) and arbitrary admissible even \(G\), including fixed \(G\), suppose separately that
\[
B^{-1}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_B}\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}\to_P\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}.
\]
Then
\[
\widehat\Gamma=\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}+B^{-1}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_B}D_b+o_P(1).
\]
Both \(\widehat\Gamma_b\) and \(D_b\) are uniformly bounded in Frobenius norm, and every probability limit point of \(\widehat\Gamma\) dominates \(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}\) in Loewner order.  If, in addition, \(\lambda_{\min}(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}})>0\), then clipping is inactive with probability tending to one and \(\|\widehat\Gamma_+^{-1}\|=O_P(1)\).

review.note: Lean implies the paper-domain claim, but the paper does not imply Lean: the theorem quantifies over arbitrary N-indexed model structures without requiring the predictable soft two-stage law or B_N→∞, and the structures do not tie design, pi, or piPair to that law; add those design constraints and restrict the asymptotic clauses to B_N→∞ sequences with shared fixed regularity and clipping parameters.

nl.statement:
Along every sequence in \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\) with \(B\to\infty\) and arbitrary admissible even \(G\), including fixed \(G\), suppose separately that
\[
B^{-1}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_B}\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}\to_P\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\lambda_{\min}(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}})>0.
\]
Then the observable ellipse satisfies
\[
\liminf_{B\to\infty}\Pr_{\mathrm{RR}}\{\tau\in\mathcal C_\alpha\}\geq1-\alpha.
\]

review.note: Paper⇒Lean fails: `Mdl.design` is an arbitrary `FiniteDesign` with no S-2 soft-rerandomization-law constraint, and `(Mdl N).alpha` may vary with N, so the conclusion is a moving-threshold bound rather than the fixed-α liminf claim; constrain the design sequence to `P_RR` and bind one fixed α with `(Mdl N).alpha = α`.

nl.statement: On the boundary extension \(\eta=1\), or equivalently when \(\kappa=0\), \(f_{\eta,\kappa}\equiv1\), \(P_{\mathrm{RR},b}=P_0\), \(v_{\eta,\kappa}=1\), and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{CR}}\); the estimator and studentizer reduce to the ordinary balanced two-stage Horvitz--Thompson construction.

review.note: Paper ⇒ Lean's boundary weight, zero projection-gain, and first-stage constant-tilt identities, but Lean ⇏ paper because it omits Ω_RR = Ω_CR and the reductions of jointHTEstimator and completedStudentizer to their ordinary balanced two-stage Horvitz–Thompson counterparts.

nl.statement: The family \(\mathcal W^{AB}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\), its type A and type B imbalance variances converge to \(53/16\) and \(29/16\), and \[P=\frac12\left\{\frac1{53}\begin{pmatrix}36&6\\6&1\end{pmatrix}+\frac1{29}\begin{pmatrix}4&10\\10&25\end{pmatrix}\right\}\succ0.\] Thus the design is genuinely adaptive through prior observed outcomes and every nonzero joint contrast is strictly improved.

review.note: Paper→Lean fails because the witness variances only converge (the finite-G formulas include G/(G-1), history-dependent A-block terms, and a distinct initialization block), whereas Lean requires exact 53/16 and 29/16 values for every N and history without G,B→∞; Lean→paper fails because the endpoint equality and one pair of worlds with differing observed outcomes and assignments neither identify Mdl.design with softTwoStageDesign nor establish dependence of its conditional law on prior outcomes (and Lean also omits λ=1). Re-scaffold with the actual W^{AB} soft-design linkage, λ=1, the stated growth regime and variance convergence, and a genuine history-dependent conditional-law assertion.

nl.statement: Let \(\{\xi_{Tt},\mathcal F_{Tt}:1\leq t\leq T\}\) be a square-integrable martingale-difference array, let \(\mathcal V_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbb E(\xi_{Tt}^2\mid\mathcal F_{T,t-1})\), and let \(V_T=\mathbb E(\mathcal V_T)\). If \(\mathcal V_T/V_T=1+o_P(1)\) and, for every \(\epsilon>0\), \(V_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbb E[\xi_{Tt}^2\mathbf1\{|\xi_{Tt}|\geq\epsilon V_T^{-1/2}\}]=o_P(1)\), then \(V_T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_{Tt}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\).

review.note: The frozen cited theorem uses an unnormalized array, trivial F_T0, V_T = E(𝒱_T), the stated V_T-dependent truncation threshold, and V_T-normalized conclusion; Lean instead assumes an already unit-normalized array, fixed-threshold conditional Lindeberg sums, and no trivial-initial-filtration condition, so neither reparameterization direction is established.

nl.statement:
There exists a deterministic sequence \(\varepsilon_G\downarrow0\) such that, uniformly over blocks, histories, and members of \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\),
\[
\left|\mathbb E_0f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)-\mathbb Ef_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b^\star)\right|
+\left\|\mathbb E_0[A_bA_b^\top f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)]-\mathbb E[A_b^\star A_b^{\star\top}f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b^\star)]\right\|
\leq\varepsilon_G,
\]
and
\[
\left\|\mathbb E_0[R_bR_b^\top f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)]-\mathbb E[R_b^\star R_b^{\star\top}f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b^\star)]\right\|
\leq\varepsilon_G.
\]
The comparison is on the exact covariance range and remains valid when the score covariance is singular; no positive lower bound on either score-coordinate variance is required.

review.note: Paper ⇒ Lean fails: after unfolding, all discrete moments and covariance matrices use the unconstrained field `Mdl.design : FiniteDesign (O N)` (tagged as the rerandomized law), while the paper requires the uniform balanced-sign benchmark P₀ conditional on the prior history; `x_balanced` restricts realized sign vectors but neither fixes their probabilities to P₀ nor supplies the conditioning, so re-scaffold every comparison using the exact history-indexed P₀ law.

nl.statement:
For the arrays generated by \(\texttt{def:adaptive-witness}\), using only their displayed bounded construction and the conditional design in \(\texttt{def:soft-two-stage-design}\), uniformly over \(b\in\mathcal B_B\) and every realized history through block \(b-1\),
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_0f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)-\mathbb Ef_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b^\star)\right|
 +\left\|\mathbb E_0\{A_bA_b^\top f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)\}
 -\mathbb E\{A_b^\star A_b^{\star\top}f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b^\star)\}\right\|
 \longrightarrow0
\]
as \(G\to\infty\).  The comparison uses the exact covariance range and requires no lower bound on a score-coordinate variance.  Moreover, without using a covariance-stabilization or model-class premise,
\[
 \left\|\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}-\Sigma_{b,0}
 +(1-v_{\eta,\kappa})\beta_b\beta_b^\top\right\|\longrightarrow0.
\]

review.note: Lean ranges over merely positive n and possibly empty B and concludes bounds only for custom first-stage witness covariances, whereas the paper ranges over the admissible 4-divisible group sizes and positive block counts and asserts the actual soft-two-stage Σ_b,RR, Σ_b,0, and β_b quantities; require 4 ∣ n N and 0 < B N and encode or state the bridges to the tilted first-stage plus fixed-count second-stage design.
